canvas-08.description: Printed sheet 3 shows the northwest corner of the Jersey City Heights block pattern between Tonnele Avenue along the bottom edge and the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad (here also lettered Paterson and New York, and Hudson River) curving across the top. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs down the left side beside Newark Avenue. From left to right the long streets are Newark Avenue, Cherry Lane, Dey Street and St. Paul's Avenue, all running up the page from Tonnele Avenue; Covert Street, Larch Avenue, Seaman Avenue and Van Wagenen Avenue cross the right-hand blocks, which are cut off on the east by an oblique sheet boundary marked 'See Sheet 4'. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Most of the area is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings, coal yards and sheds along Tonnele Avenue and Newark Avenue, a pottery near the railroad cut, and several large undeveloped blocks (613, 613 1/2) with a single house. Richards Place is a row of small dwellings on lots facing a short street. East of St. Paul's Avenue, blocks 636 to 640 are closely lotted with rows of two- and three-storey dwellings, crossed by a diagonal strip lettered Jersey City Water Works (a pipe line right of way). Adjoining sheets are indicated by small numbers (2, 4, 6, 7) at the margins.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is Tonnelle Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Cherry Lane is Van Winkle Avenue today.
Richards Place lies along the line of modern Senate Place (not confirmed by name).
Larch Avenue, Seaman Avenue and Van Wagenen Avenue east of St. Paul's Avenue are no longer present at this position; the area is cut by US 1 and 9.
Street lines from the Newark Avenue corner to St. Paul's Avenue fit modern Newark Avenue, Dey Street and Saint Paul's Avenue within about 3 m.

Printed sheet 3 (cleaner of two scans; canvas sheet-3 skipped). 50 ft. Tonnele Av to Covert St; Newark Av, Cherry Lane (= Van Winkle Av), Dey St, St. Paul's Av; Larch, Seaman, Van Wagenen, Richards Pl (gone). One part.

sheet-1.description: Printed sheet 1 is the northwest corner of the volume, where the grid of the Jersey City Heights meets the Hackensack River. Duffield Avenue crosses the sheet near the top and Charlotte Avenue runs along the bottom, with Bogart Avenue and Halsey Avenue between them. The north-south streets are Newark Avenue beside the Pennsylvania Railroad on the left, Howell Street, St. Paul's Avenue and Meadow Street, with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) running down the right margin. A strip lettered Jersey City Water Works crosses the left blocks, and a second diagonal line crosses the lower left block 607. Almost the whole area is laid out in lots but unbuilt: blocks 605 to 607, 647, 649, 651 and 655 to 657 show lot lines with only a few scattered sheds and dwellings near St. Paul's Avenue, while the larger tracts north of Duffield Avenue (blocks 602, 603, 652 and 654) run to the river. The one industrial site is a yard north of Duffield Avenue with long storage sheds and an office, and a few small buildings stand beside the river bank. The Hackensack River and its tidal edge are drawn in blue across the top. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, not 50, with north towards the upper right. The blank outlined blocks along the left margin and the bottom edge belong to Volume 5 and to sheet 2.
notes: The printed scale is 1 inch = 60 feet, not 50 feet.
Duffield Avenue, Howell Street and St. Paul's Avenue north of Charlotte Avenue exist today but their modern junction nodes lie 12 to 19 m from the drawn ones, so they are not used as control.
Bogart Avenue, Halsey Avenue and Meadow Street no longer exist at this position (Meadow Street may be today's Van Keuren Avenue).
The part is placed from one junction (Charlotte Avenue and St. Paul's Avenue) and block corners carried from sheet 2; low confidence.

60 ft (printed). Duffield, Bogart, Halsey, Charlotte Avs, Newark Av, Howell St, St. Paul's Av, Meadow St; mostly unbuilt lots by the Hackensack River. One part, anchored on Charlotte / Saint Paul's plus two corners carried from sheet 2; Duffield Av junctions 15-19 m off (realigned), left out.

sheet-2.description: Printed sheet 2 lies directly south of sheet 1 and shows the first built-up blocks of the Jersey City Heights west of the Hackensack meadows. Charlotte Avenue runs along the top and Covert Street along the bottom, with Amelia Street, James Avenue, Lewis Avenue and West Side Avenue between them. The north-south streets are Newark Avenue on the left, beside the Pennsylvania Railroad, then Cherry Lane, Howell Street, Dey Street, St. Paul's Avenue and Meadow Street, with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) down the right margin. Blocks 598 to 600 and 608 to 610 on the left are lined with frame dwellings and a few brick buildings, and the E. and H. Anthony Company photographic chemical works and other shops stand on block 643. A gas works with a gasometer occupies the upper right block 658 on St. Paul's Avenue, and the closely lotted blocks 662 and 664 between James Avenue and West Side Avenue hold dwellings, a woodworking mill and a locomotive house at the edge of the railroad yard. The tracks of the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad and of the Paterson and Hudson River line sweep in a curve across the bottom of the sheet, with a coal yard beside them. A diagonal strip lettered Jersey City Water Works crosses blocks 643 and 644. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: The printed scale is 1 inch = 60 feet, not 50 feet.
Cherry Lane is Van Winkle Avenue today.
West Side Avenue is Westside Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Amelia Street, Covert Street and Meadow Street are not placed from control points; Covert Street and Meadow Street are not used because the modern lines are displaced from the drawn ones.
Control on the west side (Newark Avenue, Howell Street, Dey Street) is hand-picked; the east side rests on St. Paul's Avenue junctions.

60 ft (printed). Charlotte Av to Covert St; Newark Av, Cherry Lane (= Van Winkle Av), Howell, Dey, St. Paul's, Meadow; gas works, NYS&W yard. One part; Covert St (about 10 m off) and Meadow St left out.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows railroad land and open ground north-west of Tonnele Avenue on the western edge of Jersey City Heights, between the end of Covert, Larch, Seaman and Van Wagener Avenues on the left and the Newark and Hudson Railroad on the right. Across the top run the many tracks of the New York, Susquehanna and Western Rail Road and the Paterson and Hudson River Rail Road. Two branches of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, one lettered Morris and Essex Division, curve down through the middle of the sheet towards Tonnele Avenue, which they pass under at a bridge; block 690 lies between them. To the right, Utica Street runs from Tonnele Avenue up to the railroads past St. Peters Catholic Cemetery, which fills most of block 961, and the Newark and Hudson Railroad and the N.Y.L.E. and W. Railroad cross the lower right corner towards Tonnele Avenue. The only works shown are the Trinidad Asphalt Paving Company's yard near Larch Street, with open sheds, a boiler house and a brick building, and a few dwellings along the dividing line with sheet 3. The strip of the Jersey City Water Works crosses the lower left corner towards Hopkins Avenue, which leaves Tonnele Avenue towards sheet 8. Most of the sheet is blank paper: it is an outlying sheet with little built on it. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, and outlines the edges of sheets 3, 5, 8 and 32.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is today's Tonnelle Avenue (US 1 and 9); Hopkins Avenue no longer reaches it.
Van Wagener Avenue is lettered Van Wagenen Avenue on sheet 3.

Placed from Tonnelle Avenue / Utica Street (hand-picked) and two points carried from sheet 8 (Hopkins Avenue / Tonnele Avenue and the Morris and Essex bridge), all along Tonnele Avenue (helmert); low to medium confidence.

50 ft. Rail lines (NYS&W, P&HRR, DL&W Morris & Essex, Newark & Hudson) and St. Peters Catholic Cemetery north of Tonnele Av (= Tonnelle Av); Utica St; ends of Covert, Larch, Seaman, Van Wagener Avs. One part, helmert on Tonnelle/Utica (hand-picked) plus Hopkins/Tonnele and the M&E bridge carried from sheet 8 (rot 62.6).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the Erie Railroad yards north of Tonnele Avenue in Jersey City Heights, between the Newark and Hudson Railroad on the left and Manhattan Avenue on the right. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad and the Paterson and Hudson River Railroad run across the top, with the Northern Railroad of New Jersey joining them on the right, and the wide fan of Erie Railroad tracks crosses the sheet diagonally. The Erie Railroad round house and turntable stand at the left, with coal pockets beside the tracks and a coal trestle and further coal pockets near Manhattan Avenue. Ledoux and Company's ore sampling works, with a crusher and engine house, lie beside the tracks near Tonnele Avenue. On the right, Allen Street, Carleton Street and Beach Street run up from the avenue between blocks 971, 972 and 973, which are laid out in lots but have only a few buildings, among them a large building for mushroom cultivation and a long shed with a note on its foundation. Stagg Street and Cliff Street leave the avenue towards sheet 8, and the edges of sheets 8, 9, 33 and 35 are outlined. Tonnele Avenue itself is lettered at the left and crosses the bottom of the sheet diagonally as the avenue. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is today's Tonnelle Avenue (US 1 and 9); Stagg Street and Cliff Street no longer reach it (they now begin at Liberty Avenue, the old Germania Avenue of sheet 9).
Carleton Street is today's Carlton Avenue.
Allen Street no longer exists.

Placed from three hand-picked Tonnelle Avenue junctions and three junctions carried from sheet 9 (Stagg, Cliff, Allen Streets at Tonnele Avenue), all along one line (helmert); low to medium confidence.

50 ft. Erie Railroad yard and round house north of Tonnele Av (= Tonnelle Av, not Liberty Av: Germania Av of sheets 8-9 is Liberty Av); Allen (gone), Carleton (= Carlton Av), Beach Sts, Manhattan Av. One part, helmert on three hand-picked Tonnelle junctions plus Stagg, Cliff, Allen / Tonnele carried from sheet 9.

sheet-6.description: Printed sheet 6 covers the blocks between Tonnele Avenue at the top and Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) at the bottom, east of the broad Pennsylvania Railroad cut that crosses the left half of the page diagonally. The two main north-south streets are Newark Avenue and Van Winkle Avenue, with Cottage Place and a short row of lots to their west; Cherry Lane enters at the top right edge from sheet 3. Germania Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, Herbert Place cuts the western block, and Skillman Avenue leaves the right margin below. The blocks are numbered 586 1/2, 589, 589 1/2, 595 and 596. They are closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings in yellow, a few brick buildings in pink and sheds in grey; individual buildings are labelled for a bakery, a wagon maker and a Weiss beer works. The Pennsylvania Railroad and Hudson Boulevard curve across the lower left. The large blank area on the left carries the compass, the scale bar and a note that it is Volume 5, Sheet 33; it belongs to another volume and is not part of the part's street map. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Adjoining sheets are numbered 3, 7, 10 and 11 at the margins; street widths are lettered at the corners (50 to 100 feet) and house numbers run along every frontage.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is Tonnelle Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Germania Avenue is Liberty Avenue today.
Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Cottage Place is Cottage Street in OpenStreetMap.
The blank area at the left, marked Vol. 5 Sheet 33, belongs to another volume.
50 ft. Tonnele Av to Hudson Blvd (= JFK Blvd); Newark, Van Winkle Av, Cottage Pl (= Cottage St), Germania Av (= Liberty Av); left side blank (vol. 5), masked. One part.

sheet-7.description: Printed sheet 7 shows the first full set of residential blocks south of Tonnele Avenue, which crosses the top of the sheet on a diagonal. Three north-south streets divide the sheet: Van Winkle Avenue on the left (Cherry Lane enters from sheet 3 above Tonnele Avenue), Dey Street and St. Paul's Avenue in the middle, which bends to the upper right where it meets Tonnele Avenue, and Hopkins Avenue on the right. Three cross streets run across the page: Germania Avenue, Skillman Avenue and, along the bottom, Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue), drawn 100 feet wide. The blocks are numbered 615 to 618 on the left and 633 to 635 on the right. Development is thin on the upper blocks, with a few dwellings, a carpenter's shop and a row of frame houses facing Tonnele Avenue, while the Germania Avenue to Skillman Avenue block has a factory of Foot and Brooks, makers of polishers' materials, and Alexander Row, a terrace of pink-coloured brick dwellings. The Skillman Avenue to Hudson Boulevard block is lined with dwellings along Hudson Boulevard, and block 633 on the right is lot lines only. Adjoining sheets 3, 6, 8 and 12 are outlined at the margins as blank rectangles. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right; street widths of 50 to 100 feet are lettered at the corners.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is Tonnelle Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Germania Avenue is Liberty Avenue today.
Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
The right-hand street is lettered Hopkins at the lower end and Avenue at the upper end; the name is read as Hopkins Avenue (medium confidence).
Hopkins Avenue and the right-hand blocks are not placed from control points: only the left and middle columns carry them.
50 ft. Tonnele, Germania (= Liberty), Skillman, Hudson Blvd; Van Winkle, Dey, St. Paul's, Hopkins. One part; Hopkins third has no control.

sheet-8.description: Printed sheet 8 lies where several railroads converge north of Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue). Tonnele Avenue crosses the top; the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) runs down the page from it in a cut with a bridge over the avenue, the Erie Railroad and the Newark and Hudson Railroad cross it diagonally in a fan of tracks, and a dashed line near the bottom marks the centre line of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western railroad tunnel. West of the cut, Germania Avenue and Skillman Avenue run across blocks 689, 691 and 692, each crossed obliquely by the strip lettered Jersey City Water Works; Hopkins Avenue closes the block on the left. East of the cut are blocks 955, 956 and 957 between Elm Street, Floyd Street and Spruce Street, with a few detached dwellings at the south end of the blocks and long unbuilt lots to the north; Utica Street joins Tonnele Avenue at the top. Beacon Avenue enters from the south below Hudson Boulevard, drawn 100 feet wide. Most lots are drawn as lines only, with buildings confined to the blocks south of Germania Avenue between Elm and Spruce Streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Blank outlined blocks at the left and right edges are neighbouring sheets 7 and 9, and sheets 4, 5, 12 and 13 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is Tonnelle Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Germania Avenue is Liberty Avenue today.
Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Hopkins Avenue is lettered in two parts (Avenue at the upper end, Hopkins at the lower end); read as one street (medium confidence). It does not survive north of Collard Street.
Elm Street, Floyd Street and Spruce Street end at Hudson Boulevard on the south and at Germania Avenue on the north.
50 ft. Tonnele railroad junction, Utica, Elm, Floyd, Spruce, Beacon, Hudson Blvd, Germania, Skillman, Hopkins. One part; west part uncontrolled.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the blocks between Tonnele Avenue on the north and Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) on the south, from Spruce Street on the west to Manhattan Avenue on the east, in the Heights section of Jersey City. Tonnele Avenue crosses the top of the sheet as a wide diagonal road. Germania Avenue runs across the middle and divides the sheet into a lower row of six regular blocks (953, 951, 947, 945, 943 and 941) and an upper strip of long deep lots (954, 948A, 948, 948B and 942) running back toward Tonnele Avenue. The lower blocks are cut into narrow lots of about 25 feet; frame dwellings are drawn on blocks 953, 951, 947 and 945, mostly in the west and in the strip along the avenues, while blocks 943 and 941 are blank lot lines with no buildings, and block 941 is one large undivided lot. The upper blocks are almost empty apart from a row of small buildings along Germania Avenue on block 954 and a long low building, labelled in small lettering, in the upper middle, on block 948. A large part of the northeast, block 942, is a single unsubdivided tract. Streets are 60 feet wide except Germania Avenue and Hudson Boulevard, which are drawn wider. Allen Street is shown only as a short street at the top, between the neighbouring sheet 5 and Tonnele Avenue. A compass and scale bar sit at the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is rotated about 60 degrees, so that the streets run up and to the right. Adjoining sheets 8, 5, 35, 37, 13 and 41 are named at the edges.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is marked 'formerly Nelson Avenue'; modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Germania Avenue is modern Liberty Avenue; Tonnele Avenue is modern Tonnelle Avenue.
Carleton Avenue is modern Carlton Avenue.
Allen Street no longer exists; Stagg and Cliff Streets no longer reach Tonnelle Avenue.
Automatic detection needed ink_below_paper 100; the sheet has lot lines and no buildings on many blocks.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
50 ft. Tonnele Av / Germania Av (= Liberty) / Hudson Blvd (formerly Nelson Av); Spruce, Stagg, Cliff, Lake, Carleton, Beach, Manhattan; mostly lots. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows a residential district of Jersey City Heights between Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) along the top and Summit Avenue along the bottom, bounded on the east by Cottage Street. North on this sheet points up and to the right, so the sheet is turned about 80 degrees. Four parallel streets, Magnonlia Avenue, Pavonia Avenue, Van Reipen Avenue and Cottage Street, run from the boulevard to Summit Avenue and divide the sheet into blocks numbered 581, 582, 584, 584 1/2, 583 and 586. Wetmore Place and Homestead Place cross between them. The blocks are filled with closely spaced frame dwellings, drawn as small yellow rectangles on narrow lots, with some brick buildings in pink, several rows of attached houses in block 584 and a Baptist church at the south end of block 586, near Cottage Street. A larger group of buildings stands in the lower left on block 581, near Summit Avenue. Hudson Boulevard curves across the top of the sheet and is drawn wide, with a retaining wall or cut along its northwest side. The broad band of the Pennsylvania Railroad, with its many tracks, crosses the left of the sheet diagonally and the left third is otherwise blank, carrying a reference to Volume 6, Sheet 43. A compass and the scale bar (1 inch = 50 feet) are in the left margin. Adjoining sheets named at the edges are 6 (north), 11 (east), 14 (southwest) and 15 (south).
notes: Hudson Boulevard is marked 'formerly Nelson Avenue'; modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Magnonlia Avenue is printed with this spelling; the modern street is Magnolia Avenue.
Wetmore Place no longer exists; Homestead Place survives only as a pedestrian way.
The railroad at the left is now the Pennsylvania Railroad cut at Journal Square.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
50 ft. Hudson Blvd to Summit Av, Magnonlia (sic) Av to Cottage St; Pennsylvania RR cut at left. One part; Summit Av drawn 50 ft (street_widths).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows two long blocks of Jersey City Heights between Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) at the top and Summit Avenue at the bottom. Cottage Street bounds the left side, Newark Avenue runs down the middle, and Van Winkle Avenue, a slanting street, forms the right boundary of the mapped area. Block 588, between Cottage Street and Newark Avenue, is a single long block of narrow lots almost completely covered with frame dwellings and tenements, with some brick buildings in pink, and stables near its southern end by Summit Avenue. East of Newark Avenue the ground is cut into four blocks, 594, 593, 592 and 591, by Ferris Street, Porter Street and Frazer Place, each lined with closely built frame houses and some shops, with a long irregular lot of small buildings in block 594 near Hudson Boulevard. Jay Street forms the east side of blocks 593 to 591, and Huron Avenue leaves Van Winkle Avenue at the upper right. Newark Avenue and Hoboken Avenue diverge at the bottom of the sheet where they meet Summit Avenue. The sheet is turned about 82 degrees from north, which points to the upper right, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The right half of the sheet repeats the same blocks, with the same block numbers and street names, as plain lot lines without buildings; only the left half is the working map and the right half was left out of the georeferenced area. A compass and scale bar are at the centre of the sheet.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is marked 'formerly Nelson Avenue'; modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Ferris Street, Porter Street, Frazer Place and Jay Street no longer exist.
The right half of the sheet duplicates the left half as lot lines only and is not part of the georeferenced mask.
Fit rests on 6 points at about 3 m RMSE; Summit Avenue junctions all carry residuals of about 3 m.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
50 ft. Newark Av blocks between Hudson Blvd and Summit Av; right half repeats the left as lot lines (left half only). One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 lies in the Heights section of Jersey City and covers the area between Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) along the top and Summit Avenue along the bottom, from Van Winkle Avenue on the left to Beacon Avenue on the right. St. Paul's Avenue, a slightly bent street, runs from top to bottom through the middle, and Hopkins Avenue slants across the lower right to meet Summit Avenue. Huron Avenue crosses near the top, Collerd Street crosses the middle and Bevan Street the lower part. At the upper left, block 619 holds St. John's R.C. Church (blue), the parish school and another school, with a row of small shops along Huron Avenue below it. Between Van Winkle and St. Paul's Avenues the blocks 620 to 623 are cut by narrow alleys and lanes (Van Vort Alley, Holden Lane) and are closely built with frame dwellings, with a long row of pink brick dwellings along Huron Avenue. The lower left block, 624, is served by Jay Street, Crothers and Court and has closely built tenements and dwellings near Summit Avenue. To the east of St. Paul's Avenue, blocks 632, 631, 630, 693, 694 are large, deep lots drawn as lot lines only, with few buildings, while block 629 along Summit Avenue and block 696 beside Hopkins Avenue are lined with dwellings and shops. A dash-dot line crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right. A church stands in block 628. Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet, turned about 80 degrees so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets named are 11, 7, 8, 13, 16, 17 and 18.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is marked 'formerly Nelson Avenue'; modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Collerd Street is printed with this spelling; the modern street is Collard Street.
Ferris, Porter, Jay, Crothers, Court, Terry, Holden Lane and Van Vort Alley no longer exist; the area is now under NJ 139 and Journal Square.
Van Vort Alley, Holden Lane, Court and Fleet Street were read from the sheet at lower resolution; check the spelling.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
50 ft. Van Winkle to Beacon Av, Huron, Collerd (sic), Bevan Sts. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 is dominated by Reservoir No. 2 of the Jersey City water works, an oval basin with a pale blue water ring on the high ground of the Heights, with its compass and a diagonal footbridge or pier to the inner basin at its southwest. The map runs from Hudson Boulevard (formerly Nelson Avenue) across the top to Summit Avenue along the bottom, and from Beacon Avenue at the left to Carleton Avenue at the right edge. Collard Street bends along the north side of the reservoir, with Spruce Street meeting it from the boulevard. Blocks 841 and 842 on the north are lined with frame dwellings; blocks 843 and 845 east of the reservoir run down Lake Street to Montrose Avenue, and are densely built with dwellings along their street frontages, with a few brick buildings in pink. A group of lots in block 846 and the strip of block 844 along Troy Street at the lower right hold more dwellings and a long yellow frame building. At the lower centre, on Summit Avenue, stands the Jersey City Water Works pumping station, a large pink brick building. At the lower left, Hicks Street runs obliquely beside the reservoir, serving block 699, a row of dwellings and a tall hall or greenhouse in yellow. Laidlaw Avenue and Jefferson Avenue appear at the very bottom, beyond Summit Avenue. Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet, with north towards the upper right. Adjoining sheets named at the edges are 8, 9, 12, 18, 19 and 41.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is marked 'formerly Nelson Avenue'; modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Carleton Avenue is modern Carlton Avenue.
Hicks Street no longer exists; Laidlaw Avenue and Jefferson Avenue survive.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
Sheet 12 prints the same street as 'Collerd Street'; this sheet prints 'Collard'.
50 ft. Reservoir No. 2, Collard, Hicks Sts. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the lower southwest corner of the Heights section of Jersey City, along the Pennsylvania Railroad cut. Two parallel streets, Pavonia Avenue and Magnolia Avenue, run across the sheet, joining Summit Avenue on the left and Baldwin Avenue on the right; Willow Court enters from the top above Pavonia Avenue. North on this sheet points toward the upper left, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Block 522, between Pavonia and Magnolia Avenues, is a long block of narrow lots with a row of dwellings along each side, and a church, drawn in pink, at its west end by Summit Avenue. South of Magnolia Avenue, West Street and East Street separate blocks 521, 520 and 519, which are only partly built, with a small group of dwellings and a pink row of houses at the west end near Summit Avenue and scattered buildings to the east. The great undivided area 520 1/2 below them is open ground, bounded on the south by the multi-track main line of the Pennsylvania Railroad, which runs across the lower part of the sheet; Summit Avenue and Baldwin Avenue slant down the sides of the open ground to cross it. The right half of the sheet, to the right of a vertical dividing line, repeats the same blocks, numbered the same, as lot lines only, without buildings, and has been left out of the georeferenced mask. Adjoining sheets named are 15, 10, 24 and 22, and the lower left carries a reference to Volume 6, Sheet 43.
notes: Summit Avenue on this sheet is 50 feet wide against about 82 feet today (Summit Avenue was later widened).
West Street and East Street still exist south of Magnolia Avenue.
The right half of the sheet duplicates the left half as lot lines only and is not part of the georeferenced mask.
The Pennsylvania Railroad line at the bottom is not used for control; the modern track lies 27 to 34 m from it.
Printed scale 1 inch = 50 feet.
50 ft. Pavonia / Magnolia Avs at Summit and Baldwin; PRR at bottom (drawn 27-34 m from modern track, railroads off); right half duplicate (left half only). One part; north to the upper left.

sheet-15.description: The left half of sheet 15 covers the county buildings of Jersey City in the Heights district, between Summit Avenue and Van Reipen Avenue at the top and Baldwin Avenue at the bottom, with Pavonia Avenue down the left side and Newark Avenue down the right. Summit Avenue runs diagonally across the upper part, crossed by Van Reipen Avenue and ending at Pavonia Avenue and Central Avenue at the left; Cottage Street opens off it at the top. Along Newark Avenue the triangular block 525 is closely built with frame dwellings and a few brick buildings, and the North Hudson County Railway, elevated, crosses the sheet from its station platforms near Pavonia Avenue to Newark Avenue. Lott Street and Willow Court lie below the railway, Willow Court with a row of small frame houses. Block 523, below Willow Court, holds the Hudson County Jail, the Hall of Records, the Hudson County Court House, drawn in pink and blue, and the Freeholders' office; a bowling alley and a wood worker's shop stand at the rear of neighbouring lots. Between the Court House and Baldwin Avenue the block is lined with dwellings on Pavonia Avenue and Newark Avenue. Cook Street and Oakland Avenue open off Newark Avenue to the right, and blocks 10, 11, 14, 16, 24 and 25 are outlined and numbered only. Street widths of 40 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Cook Street, Lott Street and Willow Court are not in the OpenStreetMap extract and are not used as control.
Hudson County Jail, Hall of Records and Hudson County Court House stand on block 523.
The North Hudson County Railway is drawn as elevated across the middle of the sheet.
50 ft. County buildings (jail, court house); right half duplicate (left half only). One part.

sheet-16.description: The left half of sheet 16 covers the junction of Summit Avenue, Newark Avenue and Hoboken Avenue at the western edge of the Jersey City Heights, and Central Avenue, which runs down the right side of the sheet. Block 571, a long rectangle between Fleet Street at the top and Hoboken Avenue, is built up along its Summit Avenue and Hoboken Avenue frontages with frame dwellings, shops and stables, including a printer, a livery stable and a short terrace called French Row, with open lots behind. Below Hoboken Avenue the triangular block 526 lies between Hoboken Avenue, Newark Avenue and Central Avenue and holds a mixed row of brick and frame buildings, among them the Avenue House with its hall and lodge rooms at the apex, a coal yard with coal sheds, and larger brick buildings near the foot of the triangle. The North Hudson County Railway runs on its elevated structure down the middle of Central Avenue, drawn as parallel lines, with the station platform at Fleet Street and a curve of tracks sweeping into Newark Avenue at the bottom; Cook Street and Willow Court are lettered on the street at the lower right. The dashed centre line of the Erie Railroad tunnel crosses the top of the sheet and block 571. A fire alarm box is marked at the apex of block 526. Blocks 11, 12, 15, 17, 20 and 25 are outlined and numbered only. Street widths of 50 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners, with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Jay Street, Cook Street and Willow Court are not in the OpenStreetMap extract and are not used as control.
Central Avenue south of Hoboken Avenue is lettered Cook Street and Willow Court on this sheet.
The Erie Railroad tunnel centre line is drawn dashed across the top of the sheet.
The control is weak: only three street junctions were detected, and the modern Central Avenue and Newark Avenue junction was not found.
50 ft. Summit / Newark / Hoboken, Central Av; right half duplicate (left half only). One part, exact fit on three points (weak).

sheet-17.description: The left half of sheet 17 covers the blocks of the Jersey City Heights where Summit Avenue, running diagonally across the upper part of the sheet, meets Fleet Street, St. Paul's Avenue and Hopkins Avenue. Central Avenue bounds the sheet at the bottom. Blocks 572 and 573 lie west of St. Paul's Avenue and blocks 574 and 575 between St. Paul's Avenue and Hopkins Avenue, with Perry Street crossing between the upper and lower pairs. Block 572 is dominated by the long yellow car house of the North Hudson County Railway, with a stable and feed store beside it; Engine Company No. 7 and its stable stand on Summit Avenue at St. Paul's Avenue, with a fire alarm box nearby; and the Simpson M.E. Church is drawn in block 573 near Central Avenue. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings in yellow, with sheds and stables at the rear of the lots, and house numbers are lettered along each frontage. A dashed line marks the Erie Railroad tunnel running up the sheet through blocks 572 and 573. Terry Alley, a narrow lane, runs off Summit Avenue to the north, and St. Paul's Avenue continues north beyond Summit Avenue. Blocks 12, 16, 18 and 20 are outlined and numbered only. Street widths of 50 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners, with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch; its north arrow points to the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
St. Paul's Avenue is Saint Pauls Avenue in OpenStreetMap, which also has a short Saint Paul's Avenue near Bevan Street.
Terry Alley is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is not used as control.
The Erie Railroad tunnel centre line is drawn dashed through blocks 572 and 573.
The car house of the North Hudson County Railway occupies much of block 572.
50 ft. Summit Av diagonal, St. Paul's, Perry, Fleet, Central; car house block 572; right half duplicate (left half only). One part.

sheet-18.description: The left half of sheet 18 covers three long blocks of the Jersey City Heights between Summit Avenue along the top and Central Avenue along the bottom, separated by Hopkins Avenue, Beacon Avenue, Laidlaw Avenue and Jefferson Avenue running down the sheet. Blocks 576 and 577 are closely built with frame dwellings in yellow, brick buildings in pink and grey and green sheds at the rear of deep lots, with a butcher and a bakery among the corner buildings and house numbers lettered along every frontage. Block 837, on the right, is occupied by W. O. Davey and Son's Paper Board and Oakum Mills: the lettered pink buildings include a paper board and finishing room, machine house, dry houses, oakum factory, boiler house, engine room, warehouse and store house, with a drying platform and paper stock house, and an air shaft is marked in front of the works. Hicks Street opens off Summit Avenue to the north, and Perry Street runs off the left margin near the lower left. A dashed line crossing the sheet marks a railroad tunnel. The platforms of the elevated railway station are drawn in Central Avenue near Beacon Avenue and again near Jefferson Avenue, and fire alarm boxes are marked at Central Avenue. Neighbouring blocks 12, 13, 17, 19, 20 and 21 are outlined and numbered only. Street widths of 50 to 60 feet are lettered at the corners with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, with the mill buildings in outline; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks (lot lines, mill buildings in outline); only the left half is georeferenced.
Hicks Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; it is not used as control.
The Summit Avenue junctions fit 1.2 to 2.4 m, looser than the Central Avenue ones (0.4 to 0.9 m); Summit Avenue bends on this sheet.
W. O. Davey and Son's Paper Board and Oakum Mills occupy block 837.
50 ft. Hopkins to Jefferson Av, Summit and Central; Davey paper mills; right half duplicate (left half only). One part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows the single large block 835 of the Jersey City Heights between Summit Avenue along the top and Central Avenue along the bottom, bounded on the west by Jefferson Avenue and on the east by Manhattan Avenue. Almost all of it is the water department's Reservoir No. 3: the basin is drawn as a pale blue band with rounded corners in the western half, with a gate house marked on its north side and a small building at the south-west corner, and the eastern half of the block is open ground with a police patrol stable standing on Central Avenue near Ferry Street. Along the top, Troy Street, Carleton Avenue and Sandford Place open off Summit Avenue to the north. Along the bottom, Waverly Street, Prospect Street, Reservoir Avenue, Booraem Avenue and Ferry Street open off Central Avenue to the south, and the platforms of the elevated railway station are drawn in Central Avenue at Reservoir Avenue. The blocks beyond the sheet are outlined and numbered only (13, 41, 18, 47, 21, 30 and 52). Summit Avenue bends where the reservoir's north-west corner is cut off, and Troy Street and Sandford Place run at an angle to the grid. Street widths of 50 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners, with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is a single map drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right; unlike neighbouring sheets it has no duplicated right half.
notes: Carleton Avenue is today's Carlton Avenue; Sandford Place is today's Sanford Place.
Reservoir Avenue is not listed in the config because it is the same OpenStreetMap node as Troy Street at Summit Avenue.
Manhattan Avenue has two stretches side by side in OpenStreetMap near Central Avenue; both junctions fitted within 1.1 and 1.8 m.
Sandford Place at Summit Avenue was not detected.
50 ft. Reservoir No. 3; single map. One part.

sheet-20.description: The left half of sheet 20 covers a strip of the Jersey City Heights between Beacon Avenue at the top and Hoboken Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the west by Central Avenue and on the east by Oakland Avenue. Four blocks are drawn, numbered 569, 568, 567 and 566 from the top, separated by Hopkins Avenue, St. Paul's Avenue and Fleet Street. The blocks are built up with frame dwellings in yellow and a few brick buildings in pink, with grey stables and sheds at the rear of the lots and house numbers lettered along each frontage. Public School No. 6 fills much of block 568 on the Central Avenue side, and block 566, the long wedge between Central Avenue and Hoboken Avenue, carries a row of pink brick dwellings along Central Avenue and St. Mary's P.E. Church near Hoboken Avenue. The platforms of the elevated railway station are drawn in Central Avenue at Beacon Avenue, at Fleet Street and at Hoboken Avenue, and the dashed centre line of the Erie Railroad tunnel crosses the lower left of the sheet and block 566. Blocks west of Central Avenue (sheets 16 and 18) and east of Oakland Avenue (sheets 25 and 27) are left blank except for their outlines and block numbers. Street widths are lettered at the corners (50 to 70 feet) with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
The junction of Hoboken Avenue and Oakland Avenue is not used: the modern node lies about 110 ft from the drawn junction.
Saint Pauls Avenue is the modern spelling in OpenStreetMap; the sheet prints St. Paul's Avenue.
Public School No. 6 and St. Mary's P.E. Church are the notable buildings.
Erie Railroad tunnel centre line is drawn dashed across the lower part of the sheet.
50 ft. Beacon to Hoboken Av, Central to Oakland; right half duplicate (left half only). One part; Hoboken / Oakland displaced (about 110 ft), left out.

sheet-21.description: The left half of sheet 21 covers the Jersey City Heights between Prospect Street at the top and Beacon Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the west by Central Avenue and on the east by Oakland Avenue. Five blocks are drawn, numbered 708 and 727 (divided by Lienau Place), 705, 701 and 570 from the top, separated by Waverly Street, Jefferson Avenue and Laidlaw Avenue. The blocks are closely built with frame dwellings in yellow, brick buildings in pink and numerous stables and sheds in grey and green at the rear of the lots, with house numbers lettered along every frontage. An oil pressing and candle factory stands on Waverly Street opposite Lienau Place. The platforms of the elevated railway stations are drawn in Central Avenue at Jefferson Avenue and at Beacon Avenue, and the dashed centre line of the Erie Railroad tunnel crosses block 705 with a small ventilating shaft marked on it. Blocks 18, 19 and 30 to the west and north, and 27, 28 and 29 to the east, are shown by outline and number only. Fire alarm boxes are marked at Prospect Street and Laidlaw Avenue. Street widths are lettered at the corners (50 to 70 feet) with water-pipe sizes at the crossings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Lienau Place is Lineau Place in OpenStreetMap.
Jefferson Avenue at Oakland Avenue was not detected.
Erie Railroad tunnel centre line is drawn dashed across block 705.
50 ft. Prospect St to Beacon Av, Central to Oakland, Lienau Pl (= Lineau Pl); right half duplicate (left half only). One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the south-western corner of the Jersey City Heights, where the grid of streets laid out around Chestnut Avenue and Waldo Avenue meets the cut of the Pennsylvania Railroad. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points towards the upper right. Two rows of blocks fill the right-hand two thirds of the sheet. The upper row lies between Baldwin Avenue and Chestnut Avenue (blocks 514, 515 and 516), is partly built with frame dwellings along Henry Street and the avenue frontage, and is crossed by the broad railroad cut. The lower row lies between Chestnut Avenue and Waldo Avenue (blocks 507, 508, 510 and 511) and is cut by First, Second, Third and Henry Streets. Block 511 next to Magnolia Avenue carries rows of brick and frame houses; block 510 holds a Greek church and the railroad right of way, and blocks 507 and 508 are largely open lots with a few houses along Second and Third Streets. The Pennsylvania Railroad appears as a bundle of tracks curving across the left side of the sheet from the lower left to the top near Baldwin Avenue, with a second line of tracks, lettered Railroad, running north through the upper blocks. The left third of the sheet is blank paper with a compass rose and the edges of Volume 6 sheets 43 and 52 outlined. Neighbouring sheets 14, 23 and 24 are named at the borders.
notes: Second Street and Third Street on Waldo Avenue are today's Trenton Street and Elizabeth Street.
Chestnut Avenue is lettered Chestnut Avenue on the sheet; the modern node Chestnut Street meets it at Vine Street.
First Street is not in the modern street network of OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is split from sheet 24 at Magnolia Avenue, which is drawn on both.
50 ft. Baldwin, High, Henry, Vine, Chestnut; First, Second (= Trenton), Third (= Elizabeth) Sts at Waldo Av. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the Pennsylvania Railroad's Waldo Avenue yard and the land around it at the southern edge of Jersey City Heights, south of Waldo Avenue between Academy Street on the left and Newark Avenue on the right. The yard fills the left half of the sheet with a wide fan of tracks, a large circular Pennsylvania Railroad round house with turntable, a store house, pump house, coal shed, coal pockets, Pullman buildings and other railroad buildings. The National Docks Railroad crosses the upper left corner, the Pennsylvania Railroad main line and its Harsimus Branch run down through the centre, and the New Jersey Junction Railroad crosses the lower right towards Newark Avenue. Along Waldo Avenue at the top are the ends of First, Second and Third Streets, Henry Street and Magnolia Street, with a few frame buildings. On the right, block 502 holds the Jersey City Cemetery, with a row of dwellings and stores along Newark Avenue; beyond Newark Avenue are Bridge Street, Seventh Street and Eighth Street. At the lower left are Fremont Street, Prior Street and Railroad Avenue, with the Nat. Docks and N.J. Junction Railroad under construction. The areas beyond the volume are marked as Volume 1 sheet 29, Volume 2 sheet 34 and Volume 6 sheets 52 and 58, and sheets 22, 24 and 26 are outlined. This sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, not 50 like most of the volume, with north towards the upper right.
notes: Scale 1 inch = 60 feet.
Second Street is today's Trenton Street and Third Street today's Elizabeth Street (by spacing along Waldo Avenue from Henry Street); First Street no longer reaches Waldo Avenue.
Magnolia Street is today's Magnolia Avenue.
Pennsylvania Railroad round house and Waldo Avenue yard.

60 ft to an inch (printed). Pennsylvania RR Waldo Avenue yard and round house, Jersey City Cemetery. Waldo Av with First (gone), Second (= Trenton St), Third (= Elizabeth St), Henry, Magnolia Sts; Newark Av, Seventh, Eighth, Bridge Sts. North about 42 deg. One part.

sheet-24.description: The left half of sheet 24 covers part of the Jersey City Heights where Baldwin Avenue, Chestnut Avenue and Waldo Avenue cross Magnolia Avenue and Pavonia Avenue, with the broad diagonal line of Newark Avenue forming the eastern edge of the built blocks. Two rows of blocks are drawn. The upper row, between Baldwin and Chestnut Avenues, holds block 517, with St. Joseph's R.C. Cathedral and St. Joseph's School at its upper end and rows of frame dwellings behind, and block 518, whose long frontage on the diagonal avenue is closely built with frame and brick houses and stables. The lower row, between Chestnut and Waldo Avenues, holds block 512, a long block of frame dwellings along Magnolia Avenue with a few brick buildings, and the small wedge-shaped block 513 between Pavonia Avenue and Newark Avenue, which includes a manufactory of knit goods. Street widths of 50, 60 and 70 feet are lettered at the corners. Palisade Avenue and McPherson Place leave Newark Avenue towards the east, where the neighbouring sheets 25 and 26 are named. Sheets 14, 15, 22 and 23 are named around the borders. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same blocks as lot lines only, without buildings, and is not part of this annotation.
notes: The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Newark Avenue is lettered in two parts on the sheet (Newark, and Avenue further along the same street); Magnolia and Pavonia Avenues are likewise lettered in parts.
The junction of Palisade Avenue and Newark Avenue was left out of the fit because it lay 4.3 m from the fit of the other junctions.
50 ft. Baldwin, Magnolia, Pavonia, Chestnut, Waldo, Newark, Palisade; right half duplicate (left half only). One part; Palisade / Newark left out (4.3 m).

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the centre of the Jersey City Heights where Oakland Avenue, Newark Avenue and Palisade Avenue meet, between Hoboken Avenue and the railroad tunnel on the north and Newark Avenue on the south. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Along the top the Centre Line of the Erie Railroad tunnel is shown as a dashed line crossing the blocks. Block 527, west of Oakland Avenue, is closely built with brick and frame buildings, among them the Third Precinct police station and a paper box and worsted goods works. East of Oakland Avenue blocks 530 and 533 front on Hoboken Avenue and Washburn Street and hold scattered dwellings and outbuildings in deep lots. Block 529 between Washburn Street and Court House Place is largely unbuilt lot lines apart from the Oakland Avenue rink. Block 528 along Newark Avenue is drawn with a row of small brick-fronted houses and then a mix of dwellings, stables and a confectionery, with Vanburen Place and Wetmore Lane cutting into the block. Blocks 531 and 532 east of McPherson Place continue the built frontage towards Palisade Avenue. Widths of 20 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners. Sheets 15, 16, 20, 24, 26 and 27 are named at the borders.
notes: Bonner Avenue is today's Baldwin Avenue.
Cook Street, Elliot Place, Wetmore Lane and Vanburen Place are not in the modern street network of OpenStreetMap; Court House Place is cut off east of McPherson Place.
The junction of Palisade Avenue and Washburn Street was left out of the fit: its modern node lay 7 to 10 m from where the other junctions placed it.
Wetmore Lane is read from a partly cropped lettering and is medium confidence.
50 ft, north to the upper left. Central, Hoboken, Oakland, Bonner, Washburn, Court House Pl, McPherson Pl. One part; Palisade / Washburn displaced, left out.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers mostly open land at the south-eastern corner of the volume, between Newark Avenue on the left and Hoboken Avenue on the right, with Palisade Avenue running from Newark Avenue towards the upper right. Waldo Avenue and Pavonia Avenue meet Newark Avenue at the upper left, and Elliot Place, Court House Place and Washburn Street run up from Palisade Avenue to sheets 24, 25 and 27. Below Palisade Avenue lie the large blocks 545 and 547, almost empty except for a few frame dwellings and a group of brick buildings at the corner of Newark and Palisade Avenues. The New Jersey Junction Railroad and the North Hudson County Electric Railway cross the lower part of the sheet towards Hoboken Avenue, and the centre line of the Erie Railroad tunnel is marked in a dashed line from the lower left to the right edge. South of the railroads the streets of Volume 2 sheet 35 are drawn in outline only: Bridge Street, Eighth Street, Pavonia Avenue, Ninth Street, Tenth Street and 11th Street crossing Division Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north pointing almost to the right, unlike most sheets of the volume, which have north towards the upper right.
notes: Palisade Avenue / Washburn Street is drawn about 25 m from Hoboken Avenue, against 70 m today; the corner was rebuilt, and Washburn Street was not used for control.
Elliot Place no longer exists; Court House Place no longer reaches Palisade Avenue.
Division Street now ends at Eighth Street; Ninth, Tenth and 11th Streets no longer cross it.
Placed from three points (two detected, one hand-picked); an exact fit, low to medium confidence.

50 ft, turned (north about 83 deg). Open blocks 545, 547 between Newark Av, Palisade Av and Hoboken Av; New Jersey Junction RR; Division St and numbered streets of vol. 2 in outline. Washburn/Palisade displaced (corner rebuilt). One part, three points.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers a regular grid of blocks on the Jersey City Heights between Beacon Avenue on the north and Hoboken Avenue on the south, and between Oakland Avenue on the west and Palisade Avenue on the east. Bonner Avenue and Concord Street run through the middle, crossed by Hopkins Avenue, Saint Paul's Avenue and Fleet Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. The blocks, numbered 552 to 564, are mostly occupied by frame dwellings in narrow lots along Beacon Avenue and in the north-eastern blocks, while the western blocks 561 to 563 are largely open lots, apart from a planing mill of a building association in block 563. Block 557 between Bonner Avenue and Concord Street is given over to a lumber and coal yard with a long range of sheds, and block 552 has a china decorating works and a storage building. Palisade Avenue runs diagonally down the east side, separating the built blocks from a large open tract (block 551) with a few isolated houses and a church. Beyond it Hoboken Avenue and the New Jersey Junction Railroad cut run along the right edge, marked Vol. 2 sheet 39. The Centre Line of the Erie Railroad tunnel is drawn as a dashed line along the bottom. Neighbouring sheets 20, 25, 26, 28 and 31 are named at the borders.
notes: Bonner Avenue is today's Baldwin Avenue.
Palisade Avenue is lettered as a diagonal street along the east side of the built blocks.
The reading of the lumber and coal yard and the planing mill rests on small lettering and is medium confidence.
50 ft, north to the upper left. Beacon, Hopkins, St. Paul's, Fleet, Hoboken, Oakland, Bonner, Palisade. One part.

sheet-28.description: The left half of sheet 28 covers four blocks of the Jersey City Heights residential district between Oakland Avenue on the north-west and Palisade Avenue on the south-east, and between Beacon Avenue and Jefferson Avenue, with Laidlaw Avenue down the middle and Bonner Avenue crossing the blocks halfway. The blocks are numbered 565 and 702 north of Bonner Avenue and 556 and 703 south of it. They are built up mostly with two- and three-storey frame dwellings set in narrow lots, drawn in yellow, with a few brick buildings in pink and stables and outbuildings in grey at the rear of the lots. Notable buildings are the Teutonia Assembly Rooms at the corner of Oakland and Beacon Avenues, a steel laundry on Oakland Avenue at Laidlaw Avenue, a stable behind it, and a bakery with its oven on Bonner Avenue. The southern ends of the blocks towards Palisade Avenue are only partly built, with a few detached houses set back in large lots. Montague Place and Palisade Place lead off Palisade Avenue towards sheet 31, and the edges of sheets 21, 27, 29 and 31 are outlined around the part. Street widths are lettered at the corners (60 to 80 feet), with house numbers along every frontage and water-pipe sizes at the junctions. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same four blocks as lot lines without buildings; it is not part of this annotation.
notes: Bonner Avenue is today's Baldwin Avenue.
The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Teutonia Assembly Rooms at Oakland and Beacon Avenues.

Pilot. 50 ft. Oakland, Bonner (= Baldwin Av), Palisade, Beacon, Laidlaw, Jefferson Avs. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the left-half blocks as lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is configured (mask x<7150). One part.

sheet-29.description: The left half of sheet 29 shows two long blocks of the Jersey City Heights between Oakland Avenue on the north and Palisade Avenue on the south. Jefferson Avenue bounds block 706 on the west, Waverly Street divides it from block 709, and Prospect Street bounds block 709 on the east. Webster Avenue leaves Prospect Street towards the east at the upper right, and Bonner Avenue ends against Jefferson Avenue at the left edge. Both blocks are cut into narrow deep lots running across the block. Frame dwellings, drawn in yellow, line the Jefferson Avenue and Waverly Street frontages along most of the length, with a few brick buildings in pink and stables or sheds in grey at the rear of the lots; the southern ends towards Palisade Avenue are only sparsely built. A dashed line crosses both blocks diagonally from the upper left to the lower right and passes through two small square buildings, one in each block. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet are lettered at the corners. Palisade Avenue runs obliquely across the foot of the sheet, and the sheet's compass rose and scale bar sit below it. Sheets 21, 28, 30 and 31 are named at the borders. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The right half of the printed sheet repeats the same two blocks as lot lines only, without buildings, and is not part of this annotation.
notes: Bonner Avenue is today's Baldwin Avenue.
The right half of the printed sheet is a second drawing of the same blocks with lot lines only (no buildings); only the left half is georeferenced.
Jefferson Avenue is drawn 60 feet wide north of Oakland Avenue and 80 feet wide south of it, with a jog of about 17 feet at the junction; the Jefferson and Oakland junction was left out of the fit.
The diagonal dashed line across the blocks is probably the centre line of the Erie Railroad tunnel, as lettered on sheets 25 and 27; its label was not read on this sheet.
50 ft. Oakland, Jefferson, Waverly, Prospect, Palisade, Webster; right half duplicate (left half only). One part; Jefferson / Oakland jog left out.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the district of the Jersey City Heights around Webster Avenue, Reservoir Avenue and Prospect Street, running from Central Avenue on the west to Palisade Avenue on the east. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Two rows of regular blocks, numbered 710 to 721, lie between Reservoir Avenue and Prospect Street and between Reservoir Avenue and Ravine Avenue, cut by Nesbitt Street, Lienau Place, Oakland Avenue and Webster Avenue. They are filled with frame and brick dwellings in narrow lots, some stables and a coal shed, and on the east side a church and a club house. In the upper right the North Hudson County Railway (Elevated) comes in along Ravine Avenue to its depot and engine house on blocks 732 and 733, with engine sheds, an open shed and a line of tracks, beside a casino on the block to the south. New York Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally near the top right and Ferry Street and Forest Place meet Ravine Avenue at the top. Booraem Avenue is lettered on both the western and eastern sides, and open ground south of Prospect Street belongs to sheets 21 and 29, which are named at the border together with 19, 31, 52 and 57. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at the corners.
notes: Lienau Place is today's Lineau Place.
Nesbitt Street, Forest Place and the part of New York Avenue shown diagonally are not in the modern street network of OpenStreetMap.
Booraem is lettered without a suffix on the west and as Booraem Ave. on the east side of the sheet.
The club house and church names in the east blocks and the casino name were not fully read.
The railway depot is lettered North Hudson County Railway Depot & Engine House.
50 ft, north to the upper left. Central, Booraem, Nesbitt, Lienau, Forest Pl, Oakland, Reservoir, Prospect, Webster, Palisade. One part.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the south-eastern edge of the Jersey City Heights, where the cross streets of the Heights end against Palisade Avenue and the ground drops to the Hoboken Avenue and railroad corridors. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, a coarser scale than most of the volume, and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. A narrow strip of built blocks, numbered 704, 718, 718 1/2, 722 and 722A, runs along the south side of Palisade Avenue from Beacon Avenue to Ravine Avenue, with frame dwellings and a hospital (Christ Hospital) at the left. Montague Place, Palisade Place and Ogden Place cut into these blocks. Below them the sheet is mostly open ground crossed by the diagonal line of Hoboken Avenue, the tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, the New Jersey Junction Railroad in its cut, and the curved line of New York Avenue. On the open ground are the stables, tanks and offices of the Standard Oil Company's Jersey City branch, and at the right the Troy Laundry Machinery Company and the Weber Cooperage Company. The lower left of the sheet is blank except for the outlines of Volume 2 sheets 39 and 44, and the lower right shows Marshall Street, Ferry Street and Jersey Avenue at the edge of Volume 7. Sheets 27 to 30, 57 and 61 are named at the borders.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch (printed scale note), not 50.
Montague Place meets Palisade Avenue but is not joined to Hoboken Avenue in the modern network.
Ogden Place and Monmouth Street are not in the modern street network of OpenStreetMap in this position.
Placement rests on junctions along Palisade Avenue only (a helmert), so the position across the sheet is the weakest.
60 ft (printed). Palisade Av strip and open ground down to Hoboken Av; helmert on Palisade Av points. One part.
